mechanism_narrative: When the Federal Funds Rate is held constant above 5.00% for two consecutive months, the S&P 500 20-day forward return is expected to be negative due to persistent higher real borrowing costs compressing equity discounting.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are non-negative in at least 70% of similar high-rate windows, or the 5.00% threshold is breached for fewer than 3 consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in monthly employment growth (PAYEMS) accompanied by a simultaneous decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) signals a labor market strengthening that boosts investor confidence and drives S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: Over a 60-day window, the 20-day ahead returns are not statistically superior to a baseline of no labor indicators change (Granger causality fails, p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly rise in retail sales (HOUST) of at least 3% for three consecutive months predicts a positive S&P 500 20-day forward return as it reflects resilient consumer demand and supports equity valuation expansion.
candidate_trigger: HOUST[t] > HOUST[t-1] * 1.03 and HOUST[t+1] > HOUST[t] * 1.03 and HOUST[t+2] > HOUST[t] * 1.03
failure_condition: In 20-day windows with similar positive HOUST momentum, forward returns are not statistically higher than during neutral momentum periods (p > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: A monthly contraction in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 2% followed within two months by a decline in consumer inflation (CPIAUCSL) below 0.5% suggests supply-side weakness that depresses equity valuations, producing negative S&P 500 5-day forward returns.
failure_condition: Over 50 such contraction episodes, the 5-day forward returns are not systematically negative (average p-value > 0.20 across t-tests).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) below 3.5% triggers a one-month spike in S&P 500 20-day forward returns as it signals labor market strength that prompts rate-cut expectations and equity optimism.
failure_condition: In 20-day windows following similar UNRATE breaks, forward returns are not statistically superior to a neutral baseline (p > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: Concurrent strength in both employment (PAYEMS) and consumer payrolls (PAYEMS) with no significant change in inflation (CPIAUCSL) creates a dual-labor signal that drives positive S&P 500 60-day forward returns by reinforcing growth expectations.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS[t] > PAYEMS[t-1] * 1.02 and PAYEMS[t+1] > PAYEMS[t] * 1.02 and CPIAUCSL[t] < CPIAUCSL[t-1] * 1.005
failure_condition: Across 10 such dual-signal events, 60-day forward returns are not statistically better than during periods of single-labor indicator movement (Granger causality fails).

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly decline in manufacturing activity (RSAFS) of 4% or more for two consecutive months predicts negative S&P 500 20-day forward returns due to persistent supply-side stress and compression of corporate earnings expectations.
failure_condition: In 20-day windows with similar RSAFS declines, forward returns are not persistently negative (average p-value > 0.30 over 5 such episodes).

mechanism_narrative: When the 3-month moving average of FEDFUNDS falls by more than 0.25 percentage points from its prior peak within a 2-month window, the S&P 500 60-day forward return is expected to be negative due to heightened risk aversion and reduced liquidity in financial markets.
failure_condition: Over 10 such 60-day windows following similar FEDFUNDS declines, forward returns are not systematically negative (average p-value > 0.20).
